tagline: A lawman’s namesake town and a dam built deep.
intro: Parker Dam Road starts at Earp, in the Sonoran Desert close to the Arizona line, and runs to the Colorado River community of Parker Dam. BLM and private campsites sit along the way. Wyatt Earp once worked more than 100 copper and gold claims near the base of the Whipple Mountains here.
The dam at the end stands 320 feet high, and 235 of those feet are below the riverbed, dug down to bedrock. In 1935 Arizona sent its National Guard to halt construction.

moments.title: Earp
moments.text: The town commemorates Wyatt Earp’s mining years, with a mock grave for a man actually buried in Colma.

moments.title: Parker Dam
moments.text: The community takes its name from the dam nearby, which holds Lake Havasu where the river passes between the Whipple and Buckskin mountains.
